claims.claim: Memory is shifting from crushing short-term numbers to long-term agreements with a floor and a ceiling, trading short-term upside for durability.
claims.prediction: Memory eps-surprise MAGNITUDE compresses faster than other layers, because contracted revenue does not surprise.
claims.why_it_matters: Our DRIVER is EPS surprise and memory is 9.8% of notional with 4 of 5 names top-14. If true we are overweight exactly where the driver stops working.
claims.metric: layers.memory.trend minus the mean trend of other layers
claims.action_if_supported: Lean the REVISIONS leg over the SURPRISE leg in memory: a raised contracted floor still shows up as a raised estimate even when it stops being a beat.

claims.claim: Whether a company beats this quarter's earnings has become far harder to predict because of alternative data; reward shifts to those who see years ahead.
claims.prediction: eps-surprise IC decays across sub-periods while the thesis leg holds; dropping W_FUND costs little.
claims.why_it_matters: W_FUND=1.0 is our driver, played with free yfinance data against firms running credit-card panels. Our own sweep already hints the theme carries the book (W_THESIS=0 collapses Sharpe 3.1 -> 1.7).
claims.metric: rank IC of z_eps by sub-period; Sharpe delta at W_FUND=0
claims.threshold: falling IC AND small Sharpe cost supports
claims.action_if_supported: Re-weight toward the thesis and revisions legs; the 'driver' label is on the wrong leg.
claims.verdict_detail: test killed after 52min; the IC loop recomputes _fund_asof per sample and needs hoisting before it can complete

claims.claim: The market rewards sellers of the shortage (semis, memory, optics) over buyers (hyperscaler capex). Sellers +107% YTD vs buyers +4%.
claims.prediction: Excluding capex spenders from the universe improves risk-adjusted returns.
claims.why_it_matters: This claim was the sole justification for barring six hyperscalers from the book for seven weeks.
claims.metric: Sharpe(ex-spenders) minus Sharpe(full universe), plus sub-period agreement
claims.threshold: > +0.10 in the full window AND a majority of sub-periods supports
claims.verdict_detail: 3.62 vs 3.56 full-window (+0.06, inside noise) and the edge sits ENTIRELY in the oldest third, gone in the two most recent (4.06 vs 4.04, then 3.55 vs 3.55)
claims.action_taken: EXCLUDE_AI_ROLES emptied 2026-08-03; GOOGL entered at rank 30

claims.claim: Land and power is the fastest path to cash-on-cash returns; energized land can explode in value. Acquired ~6GW.
claims.prediction: Tilting the book toward power/grid and neocloud improves risk-adjusted returns.
claims.why_it_matters: Power is our lightest layer at 6.4% and second-cheapest at ~29x, and Griffin plus Musk's turbine purchase point the same way.
claims.metric: Sharpe of each tilt vector vs W_LAYER_TILT=0, with sub-period thirds
claims.threshold: beats baseline in the full window AND a majority of sub-periods
claims.action_if_supported: Set W_LAYER_TILT > 0 with the winning vector.
claims.verdict_detail: every vector degrades; the DATA-DERIVED mean-reversion vector is worst (2.48 vs 2.89 baseline); power_only produces a book IDENTICAL to doing nothing, name for name

claims.claim: Regulation is the single biggest risk to the AI buildout; New York's data-centre moratorium is the first of many.
claims.prediction: A regulatory / power-permitting freeze is a material loss scenario for this book.
claims.why_it_matters: Our stress test had no such scenario, and every qualitative argument this week says ADD power exposure, which would raise this row.
claims.threshold: worse than -10% NAV makes it material
claims.action_if_supported: Treat added power exposure as raising this tail, not only as adding a cheap layer.
claims.action_taken: scenario added to the daily stress test

claims.claim: We trade 24/7 tokenized perps, so marking and risk should reflect the instrument we hold rather than the underlying close.
claims.prediction: Perp-basis NAV diverges materially from the official underlying-close track.
claims.why_it_matters: Decides the go-live marking basis, and with it whether perp betas govern hedge sizing.
claims.metric: basis_at_close_pct (like-for-like; the live figure also carries a session timing offset)
claims.action_if_supported: Decide the marking basis explicitly before capital; if perps, hedge sizing must move with it.
claims.action_taken: perp mark panel shipped alongside the official track; go-live decision documented, engine unchanged

claims.claim: Inverse-vol sizing ignores conviction: rank picks what we hold but never how much.
claims.prediction: Tilting weights toward higher-scoring names improves risk-adjusted returns.
claims.why_it_matters: Selection and sizing are separate decisions and only one of them used the signal.
claims.threshold: any tilt beating baseline in the full window and 2 of 3 sub-periods
claims.action_if_supported: Set W_SIZE_TILT to the winning level.
claims.verdict_detail: monotonic degradation 3.62 -> 3.58 -> 3.48 -> 3.28 -> 2.98; equal weight far worse at 2.81, so inverse-vol is genuinely earning its keep. Vol is forecastable, a rank signal's return is not.

note: CLAIMS REGISTER. Every external claim we have taken seriously enough to test, with the testable prediction it implies, the test that decides it, and the standing verdict. Run by research/claims_register.py. The point is that a refuted claim STAYS refuted without re-arguing it, an inconclusive one gets re-tested on a cadence instead of being forgotten, and a verdict that FLIPS raises an alert. Nothing here changes a weight; each entry records what we would do if the verdict changed, so that decision is made in advance rather than in the moment.
